answer: In scope, and the two options in the question are not exclusive -- CRM has a standard pattern for exactly this. Model the 1876 build as one E12 Production (P108 has produced -> the engine, an E22 Human-Made Object, carried out by the ironworks). For 1932, do not give the engine a second E12 Production -- P108 has produced is the property that asserts a thing came into existence through that activity, so reusing it in 1932 is precisely the 'built twice' reading the trust wants to avoid. Instead use the E80 Part Removal / E79 Part Addition pair (both subclasses of E11 Modification, siblings of E12 Production under E11): E80 Part Removal (P113 removed -> the old cast-iron beam, P112 diminished -> the engine) for detaching the cracked beam, and E79 Part Addition (P111 added -> the new steel beam, P110 augmented -> the engine) for fitting the replacement. P110 augmented and P112 diminished are both subproperties of P31 has modified, the same superproperty P108 has produced falls under -- so acting on the engine through P110/P112 keeps the 1932 event in the 'modified' branch, never re-triggering the 'produced' branch for the engine itself. This does not require pretending the new beam has no maker: the new steel beam can carry its own, separate E12 Production (P108 has produced -> beam, carried out by the second firm) without that production touching the engine's record at all -- the beam's P108 and the engine's P110/P112 are different property instances on different objects. The engine's continuous identity across the swap is exactly what CRM commits to: in thread t1170, discussing the Ship of Theseus, Martin Doerr states CRM identity for a physical object rests on continuity of coherence and functionality, not retained substance -- 'an instance of E19 with all parts replaced is identical' (as a physical object; not as an Amount of Matter). P46 is composed of can record the before/after part-whole state (engine composed of old beam vs. composed of new beam) if that level of detail is wanted.

rejected_alternatives.option: A second E12 Production of the engine itself in 1932 (P108 has produced -> engine)
rejected_alternatives.why_not: P108 has produced asserts the engine came into existence through that activity; asserting it again in 1932 is the exact 'whole engine built twice' implication the trust is trying to avoid.

E11's own scope note ties E81 to cases where the original object is destroyed and a new object with a separate identity is produced from its parts/material; here the engine is never destroyed, only one part is exchanged, so E81 does not fit.

rejected_alternatives.option: Merging E79/E80 into one class, or requiring them to be paired as a single dual event
rejected_alternatives.why_not: the SIG considered and rejected this: Issue 221 'Dual events' was closed not-accepted because there is no assumption that a removed part exists before and after removal, so Part Removal and Part Addition are correctly kept as independent, unpaired activities.

citations.quote: We definitely regard that an instance of E19 with all parts replaced is identical
